title: I2C controller (master): START / repeated START, byte write with ACK check, byte read with ACK / NACK, STOP
features: The controller role that the I2C_top target does not cover: sensor, PMIC and EEPROM control.
Byte commands: STA, then WR (send TX_DATA, ACK bit into RX_ACK) or RD (byte into RX_DATA, then ACK or NACK), then STO.
One quarter of the SCL period is PRESCALE + 1 clocks (at least 3); SCL push-pull, SDA open drain, single controller, no clock stretching.

fields.desc: quarter SCL period - 1, in clocks (reset 0x63: 100 kHz at 40 MHz)

regs.name: TX_DATA
regs.desc: Byte sent by the next WR command

fields.desc: issue the command made of the other bits
START (repeated START when the bus is held)
RD: answer NACK instead of ACK
byte read by the last RD
ACK bit after the last WR: 0 ACK, 1 NACK
between a START and a STOP

sequence: Write TX_DATA = {address, R/W}, then CMD = valid | sta | wr; wait for DONE, check RX.rx_ack.
For each data byte: TX_DATA and CMD = valid | wr (| sto on the last), or CMD = valid | rd (| nack | sto on the last) and read RX.rx_data.
notes: scl is driven push-pull and sda is open drain (it only pulls low; an external pull-up is required); both pass through unchanged.
